summary: The bill amends the Clean Air Act to allow year-round sales of E15 gasoline by removing Reid vapor pressure limits for 10-15% ethanol blends and to reform the renewable fuel standard by redefining small refining companies, ending most small-refinery exemptions after 2027, cutting their compliance obligations by 75% starting in 2028, restoring certain retired credits, and creating a capped hardship exemption for at-risk facilities.

scores.thoughts: The bill consists entirely of amendments to the Clean Air Act regarding fuel standards and the Renewable Fuel Standard. It contains no appropriations, authorizations for spending, or changes to federal expenditures.
The bill makes no changes to tax law, tax rates, credits, or revenue collection mechanisms.
No provisions relate to healthcare delivery, insurance, public health programs, or medical regulations.
The legislation addresses fuel formulation and refinery compliance under environmental statutes and has no connection to firearms policy.
No immigration, border, or visa provisions are present.
The bill contains no language concerning reproductive health services or abortion access.
No defense spending, military procurement, or national security funding authorizations are included.

The bill directly amends the Clean Air Act (sections 211(f) and 211(h)) to relax Reid Vapor Pressure limitations for E15 blends, modifies Renewable Fuel Standard small-refinery compliance obligations, and directs EPA rulemaking on fuel infrastructure. These changes adjust environmental regulatory requirements under the CAA and RFS program, constituting engagement with environmental regulation.
No provisions affect welfare programs, SNAP, Medicaid, or other safety-net entitlements.
The bill does not address schools, student aid, or education policy.
No content relates to controlled substances, decriminalization, or drug enforcement.
The legislation contains no criminal penalties, sentencing reforms, or policing provisions.
No tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export rules are altered.
The bill does not authorize new spending or revenue measures that would affect deficits or debt.
No provisions address LGBTQ legal protections or related civil rights.
The bill includes no foreign assistance authorizations or appropriations.
No election administration, voting access, or campaign finance provisions appear.
The legislation does not regulate technology companies, data privacy, or digital surveillance.
No labor, union, or workplace regulation changes are included.
The bill does not address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination law.
